name: @agent-org/plugin-github-issues
description: GitHub Issues as the tracker: the issues of one repository are read and written through GitHub's REST API with a token.

agentOrg.description: GitHub Issues: where tickets are kept and read.
agentOrg.setUp: GitHub Issues connected as the tracker

repo.explanation: The GitHub repository whose issues are the tickets, as owner/name.
repo.breaks: A value that is not owner/name is refused by name, and the board cannot read the tracker.

edit.dangerous: Another repository's issues become the tickets.

prefix.type: letters and digits, starting with a letter
prefix.explanation: The prefix of every ticket's key: issue 12 is GH-12, and its branch is gh-12.
prefix.breaks: A prefix that is not letters and digits is refused by name. Changing it renames every ticket's key, so queued runs no longer match their tickets.

edit.dangerous: Every ticket's key changes, and queued runs no longer match their tickets.

token.explanation: Where the GitHub token is read from: the macOS Keychain by service name, or a file. The token is never shown on this page.
token.breaks: A shape that is neither is refused by name, and the board cannot read the tracker.

edit.why: an object: change its path with tickets.providers.tracker.token.path

token.path.setCommand: ( umask 077; printf 'GitHub token: ' >&2; stty -echo; read -r SECRET; stty echo; printf '\n' >&2; printf '%s' "$SECRET" > {value|~/.config/agent-org/github-issues.token} )
token.path.explanation: The file the GitHub token is in: a token that can read and write the repository's issues. The file must be readable by no one else.
token.path.breaks: A wrong path means the board cannot read the tracker.

edit.note: the token file itself is never read by this page
edit.dangerous: The file the GitHub token is read from: a wrong path stops the board from reading the tracker.

token.keychain.type: service name in the macOS Keychain
token.keychain.explanation: The Keychain service that holds the GitHub token. This page names the service and does not read the token.
token.keychain.breaks: A service with no key there means the board cannot read the tracker.

edit.why: a secret's Keychain service: the ticket allows only the path to a key file to change

connectors.explanation: The connector tools a worker may call to read or comment on a tracker ticket, each a regular expression anchored at the tool's name: the tracker's own, from Linear. tickets.connectors keeps the rest.
connectors.breaks: A pattern not starting ^mcp__ is refused by name. A broad one lets a worker act in the person's connected accounts.

edit.dangerous: A broad pattern lets a worker act in the person's connected accounts.

workingState.type: a state's name in the tracker
workingState.explanation: The state a ticket moves to as a worker starts implementing it, such as "In Progress", if it has not started yet. Absent leaves its state alone. A planning run moves nothing. The ticket goes back to the state it came from when its run ends without a pull request.
workingState.breaks: A name the tracker lacks fails that move, not the run. A team with no state of that name keeps the ticket's state, and the board's log says so.

plannedState.type: a state's name in the tracker
plannedState.explanation: The state a planned ticket moves to once its plan is attached, if it has not started. A team with no state of that name keeps the ticket's state, and the board's log says so, because teams name their states differently.
plannedState.breaks: A name the tracker lacks fails that move, not the plan.

takenStates.default: the working and planned states, where they are set
takenStates.explanation: The tracker states in which a ticket another instance claimed is held in Pick: a ticket in one of them, whose latest claim in the tracker names another instance, is shown with its state and cannot be queued here. A state of the started type is always one of them, so In Progress needs no entry. A ticket with no claim, or one this instance claimed, is not taken in any state. Listing [] names none of these states.
takenStates.breaks: A name that is not a state's name is refused by name. A state left out lets another instance's ticket be queued here too.
